package_info.package_name: Unknown (malicious npm package used by Jade Sleet/TraderTraitor)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (malicious versions posted just before targeted invitations)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is explicitly crafted to deliver a second-stage malware payload to victim systems. It is distributed as a dependency in software shared through targeted social engineering campaigns. Its only function is to compromise the host by downloading and executing additional malicious code, resulting in remote code execution and system compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code invokes a shell command using child_process.exec to fetch a remote script from https://malicious-domain.com/payload.sh via curl, pipes it directly to bash for execution, and thereby achieves remote code execution on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes a shell command during the installation phase, which downloads and immediately runs a script from an external, non-standard domain. This behavior is highly indicative of an attempt to compromise the system, as it allows arbitrary code execution from an attacker-controlled source.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not execute arbitrary shell commands or download and run remote scripts during installation, especially from untrusted or undocumented domains. Such actions violate the principle of least privilege and expected package behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use postinstall scripts to download prebuilt binaries or perform setup tasks, but these actions are typically limited to trusted, official sources and are clearly documented. Downloading and executing scripts from unknown domains is not standard practice.
key_indicators: Use of child_process.exec to run shell commands during installation
Fetching and executing code from an external, non-standard domain
Presence of a postinstall script in package.json that initiates network activity
No legitimate documentation or justification for remote code execution in the package

attack_chain.action: Threat actor initiates contact with the target via social engineering (e.g., GitHub, social media).
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is invited to collaborate on a repository or sent malicious software directly.

attack_chain.action: Victim is manipulated into cloning a repository or installing software with a malicious npm dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious npm package is installed on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Malicious npm package executes postinstall script to download and run second-stage malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Second-stage malware is executed, compromising the victim's system.

behavioral_signatures: npm package executing shell commands via child_process during postinstall
Network requests to external or suspicious domains during npm install
Automatic execution of downloaded scripts or binaries as part of installation
file_indicators: package.json containing postinstall scripts that invoke shell commands
References to external domains (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com) in install scripts
Unexpected shell scripts or binaries appearing in the project directory after npm install
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with npm or the legitimate project, such as https://malicious-domain.com
Connections to infrastructure previously linked to Jade Sleet/TraderTraitor operations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that execute shell commands or initiate network requests to external domains. Flag packages that use child_process to run arbitrary commands or reference non-standard domains in their install scripts. Correlate observed domains with known malicious infrastructure and investigate any unexpected network activity or new files created during or immediately after npm install operations.
